security_audit.summary: All 35 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, inline code, repository metadata, and fixed relative documentation links. A separate medium-risk concern remains because the workflow can scale unsolicited outreach and improve filter avoidance, although it includes consent, suppression, and legal guardrails.

remediation.issue: The workflow can be used to scale unsolicited email and distribute volume across mailboxes.
remediation.suggestion: Require a documented lawful basis, verified suppression handling, provider-compliant limits, and explicit confirmation that mailbox distribution will not bypass enforcement.

semantic_findings.title: Cold-Outreach Scaling Can Facilitate Spam
semantic_findings.description: The skill plans cold-email sequences, mailbox warmup, send throttles, and volume distribution. These capabilities can scale unsolicited messaging or reduce filtering effectiveness despite included compliance safeguards.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The stated purpose and workflow clearly optimize cold-outreach volume and deliverability. Abuse intent is not explicit because the skill also requires opt-outs and lawful-basis checks.

content.value_statement: Cold outreach needs coordinated timing, reply routing, sender protection, and compliance checks. This skill produces a structured sequence and operational guardrails before sending begins.
actual_capabilities: Creates multi-step B2B outbound sequence maps with timing, goals, and exit rules.
Routes positive, objection, referral, not-now, and opt-out replies to defined actions.
Plans mailbox warmup ramps and steady-state daily sending limits.
Lists CAN-SPAM elements and flags jurisdictions that may require prior consent.
Assesses sender authentication, reputation, bounce, complaint, and consent inputs.
Produces a handoff summary for consent review, copywriting, or quality auditing.
limitations: Does not write final subject lines, email bodies, calls to action, or legal footers.
Does not provide legal advice or determine whether a specific campaign is lawful.
Does not verify live headers, consent records, DNS settings, or sending-platform data.
Does not compute the final Email Quality Score or enforce quality vetoes.

use_cases.title: Launch a New Outbound Program
use_cases.description: Build a sequence, reply routes, and mailbox ramp before contacting a defined business audience.

use_cases.title: Protect a New Sending Domain
use_cases.description: Set cautious mailbox limits and identify authentication or reputation inputs that need verification.

use_cases.title: Review Jurisdiction Guardrails
use_cases.description: Map list sources and recipient locations to consent questions, opt-out requirements, and counsel review points.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Sequence
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a four-step B2B cold-outbound sequence for [ICP]. Include timing, one goal per step, and exit rules for replies and opt-outs.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a clear sequence structure.

prompt_templates.title: Add Reply Routing
prompt_templates.prompt: Design reply triage for [offer] and [ICP]. Route positive, objection, referral, not-now, and opt-out replies to specific next actions.
prompt_templates.scenario: A sales team needs consistent reply handling.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Mailbox Warmup
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a warmup ramp for [mailbox count] mailboxes on [domain age]. Label estimates and define weekly volume, daily caps, and monitoring thresholds.
prompt_templates.scenario: An operations team is preparing a new sending domain.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Governed Outbound Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a five-step sequence for [ICP] using [list source] across [jurisdictions]. Add reply routes, suppression rules, warmup limits, and missing-input gates.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced team needs a complete plan with compliance and deliverability controls.

output_examples.input: Plan four touches for finance leaders, with two established mailboxes and a United States list.
output_examples.output: A four-step sequence lists each delay, purpose, and exit condition. A reply table stops outreach on response, bounce, or opt-out.

output_examples.input: Create a warmup plan for three mailboxes on a new domain without historical sending data.
output_examples.output: The schedule starts with low estimated daily volumes, increases weekly, and pauses increases when bounce or complaint signals exceed defined limits.

output_examples.input: Review an outbound list containing Canadian, British, and United States contacts.
output_examples.output: The guardrail section separates jurisdiction questions, marks lawful-basis evidence as required input, and sends uncertain legal conclusions to counsel.

best_practices: Provide the list source, recipient jurisdictions, mailbox count, domain age, and current reputation signals.
Confirm lawful basis and suppression status before approving any sequence for sending.
Treat warmup volumes as estimates until measured bounce, complaint, and authentication data are available.
anti_patterns: Do not continue a sequence after any reply, opt-out, hard bounce, or suppression event.
Do not rotate mailboxes or domains to bypass provider limits, filtering, or enforcement.
Do not treat operational compliance guidance as a substitute for qualified legal review.

faq.question: Does this skill send emails?
faq.answer: No. It designs the sequence, routing, warmup schedule, and guardrails but does not connect to a sending platform.

faq.question: Does it write the email copy?
faq.answer: No. It defines each step's purpose and timing, then hands copywriting to a separate creative workflow.

faq.question: Can it guarantee deliverability?
faq.answer: No. Deliverability depends on authentication, reputation, list quality, content, recipient behavior, and provider policies.

faq.question: Is the compliance guidance legal advice?
faq.answer: No. The skill identifies operational requirements and open questions. Jurisdiction-specific decisions require qualified counsel.

faq.question: What inputs produce the best plan?
faq.answer: Provide the audience, offer, list source, jurisdictions, mailbox setup, domain age, authentication status, and recent sending metrics.

faq.question: How are opt-outs handled?
faq.answer: Every branch stops immediately on opt-out and requires suppression before any later outreach.
